meta.title: Rain or Sun on Saturday?
meta.textType: functional: a weather forecast and a plan

paragraphs: On Wednesday, November eleventh, Lily, Tom, and Dad sat in the kitchen at seven o'clock. It was already dark outside. A small radio stood on the table, and Pip lay under Dad's chair. Lily had a notepad and a pencil. "On Saturday, we are going to the aquarium," she said. "I need to know the weather." "Be quiet, please," said Dad. "The forecast is starting."

"Good evening," said the presenter on the radio. "Here is the weather for the next three days." "Tonight is warm and dry." "Tomorrow, Thursday, is sunny and hot, with thirty-three degrees." "Friday is cloudy." "On Saturday, it is dry in the morning." "After two o'clock, rain is possible, with a thunderstorm in the afternoon." "The season is changing, so storms are possible." Lily wrote three lines on her notepad. "Thursday: sunny, thirty-three degrees." "Friday: cloudy." "Saturday: dry in the morning, storms after two o'clock." She drew a sun, a cloud, and a lightning bolt next to the lines.

"Will it rain on Saturday morning?" asked Lily. "Not in the morning," said Dad, "but rain is possible after two o'clock." "Take an umbrella to the aquarium." When Pip heard the word "umbrella," he ran to the door. He took Lily's yellow umbrella and dragged it across the floor. Lily laughed, and Tom pointed at the radio. "Pip is a good listener," said Tom.

"What will you do if it rains in the afternoon?" asked Tom. "If it rains in the afternoon, we will stay in the cafe," said Lily. "We will wait there, and we will be dry." Tom looked at her notes. "The forecast does not say anything about Sunday," he said. "If Sunday is dry, Ben and I are riding to the lake." "A forecast is nearly always right," said Dad, "but it can change." "Then we will listen again later," said Lily.

Lily put her notes next to her school bag. Then she picked up the yellow umbrella from the floor. "Thank you, Pip," she said. "If it rains on Saturday, we will use this umbrella." Pip wagged his tail and said, "Woof!"
